data.name: Kulbir
data.gender_notes: Kulbir is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Kulbir is a Sanskrit name derived from the Sanskrit words ‘kula’ which means ‘family’ or ‘clan’, and ‘bir’ which means ‘lord’ or ‘ruler’. It is believed that Kulbir is the name of the supreme deity who rules over the entire universe. The name Kulbir carries the meaning “The Lord of the Universe” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kulbir usually hope their child will grow to embody the lord of the universe and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of Divine Protection and Leadership
data.etymology: Kulbir belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “The Lord of the Universe.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kulbir total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kulbir is considered auspicious and symbolizes a strong connection with one's ancestry and heritage. It is a sacred name in Hindu culture and is often given to children as a testament to their family lineage and ancestral traditions. The name is also believed to bring good fortune and prosperity to the family.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Kulbir carries a deep spiritual meaning, as it is believed to represent the divine ruler of the universe. It is a reminder that ultimately, all things are governed by a higher power. The name is also thought to bring blessings and protection to the bearer, connecting them to the divine and providing spiritual guidance in their lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kulbir: The radiant guardian of the family lineage. The name Kulbir signifies one who upholds the divine flame of knowledge and virtue within the family, illuminating the way for future generations.
